state: Environment: Kitchen workspace for assembling a layered lasagna. Countertop holds: one 9x13 baking dish (greased), a pot of cooked ground beef and tomato sauce (warm, on stovetop left burner), a bowl of ricotta-spinach mixture (room temperature), a stack of no-boil lasagna noodles (12 sheets remaining), a bag of shredded mozzarella (partially used, ~2 cups left), a container of grated parmesan (~1 cup), and aluminum foil. Oven is preheated to 375°F. The baking dish currently has two complete layers assembled: bottom sauce layer, first noodle layer, ricotta-spinach layer, second noodle layer, and a meat sauce layer. During Step 3 (spreading the ricotta-spinach mixture), the spinach was discovered to be more watery than expected, releasing liquid that has pooled slightly at the edges of the dish. The ricotta layer is thinner than planned because approximately one-third of the mixture was discarded to reduce excess moisture. Goal: A fully assembled, baked lasagna with 3 complete pasta layers, each separated by alternating ricotta-spinach and meat sauce fillings, topped with mozzarella and parmesan, baked until bubbly and golden (internal temp ~165°F). Completed: step_1 greased dish and spread thin base sauce layer → even coverage achieved; step_2 placed first noodle layer (4 sheets) → slight overlap at edges noted but acceptable; step_3 spread ricotta-spinach mixture → unexpected water release from spinach, mixture discarded partially, layer is thinner than planned; step_4 placed second noodle layer (4 sheets) → noodles absorbed some pooled liquid at edges, slightly softened before baking; step_5 spread second meat sauce layer → coverage complete but thinner at edges due to absorbed liquid causing uneven surface. Available actions: (A) Add third noodle layer and continue assembly as planned — requires at least 4 remaining noodle sheets, which are available; (B) Sprinkle mozzarella and parmesan directly on current meat sauce layer and skip third pasta layer — no preconditions; (C) Blot visible pooled liquid at dish edges with paper towel before continuing — no preconditions, reversible; (D) Add an extra thin layer of meat sauce to even out the surface before placing third noodles — requires sauce remaining in pot, which is available; (E) Proceed directly to baking the current two-layer assembly — oven is ready, but lasagna would be underfilled relative to dish depth.

state: Environment: A humanoid assembly robot is working on a laptop computer at a workbench. The laptop chassis is secured in a mounting jig. The motherboard is installed and seated correctly in the chassis. The CPU is installed in socket LGA1700 and the retention bracket is locked. The thermal paste has been applied to the CPU, but the application was uneven — a blob approximately 8mm in diameter is offset 3mm to the left of center rather than centered. The CPU cooler (a 120mm tower cooler) is positioned above the CPU but not yet mounted. Four mounting screws are laid out on the tray. The RAM slots (two of four) are populated with 16GB DDR5 sticks, both clicked fully into place. The GPU bay is empty. A GPU card is in the parts bin 40cm to the right. The cable management tray holds SATA power cables, a 24-pin ATX connector (unattached), and an 8-pin CPU power cable (unattached). A torque screwdriver is in the tool rack, calibrated to 0.5 Nm. Goal: Fully assembled laptop-style workstation with all components installed, all cables connected, cooler mounted, and system ready for POST test. Completed: step_1 → chassis prepared and motherboard seated successfully; step_2 → CPU installed and retention bracket locked successfully; step_3 → thermal paste applied, but application was off-center (unexpected — dispenser nozzle slipped during application); step_4 → RAM sticks installed in slots A2 and B2, both fully seated and latched. Available actions: (A) Mount CPU cooler over current thermal paste — no preconditions unmet; (B) Remove CPU cooler thermal paste, clean with isopropyl alcohol, and reapply centered — requires IPA wipe and fresh thermal paste in supply bin, both confirmed present; (C) Install GPU into PCIe slot — no preconditions unmet, GPU is accessible; (D) Connect 24-pin ATX and 8-pin CPU power cables — no preconditions unmet; (E) Proceed directly to POST test — requires cooler mounted and all power cables connected, neither condition is currently met.
